newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT drops on Q1 net, Asia Equity say buy.
newsitem.headline: PLDT drops on Q1 net, Asia Equity say buy.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co fell five pesos to 1,550 by midsession on Monday in what analysts described as a knee-jerk reaction to its announcement of a fall in first quarter net income.
However, Philippine Asia Equity Securities Inc research head Matthew Sutherland and Eagle Equities Inc president Joey Roxas recommended a buy on the issue despite largely negative market sentiment.
"I'm quite happy with the results of PLDT. It is still one of the biggest buys in this market because it has no property and banking exposure," Sutherland said.
PLDT reported a net income of 1.28 billion pesos in the first quarter, down 1.8 percent from the year-ago 1.31 billion due to redundancy costs.
However, the firm's net operating income rose to 2.834 billion pesos in the first quarter compared with 2.361 billion in the same period last year.
"There's a good chance of a recovery in the second half which is seasonally stronger," Sutherland said.
Roxas said "I'm still a buy on PLDT."
He said he expected PLDT's proposed rate increase on local calls to offset losses it would incur on cuts in overseas call rates.
PLDT has sought approval from the Philippine National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) to restructure its rates to meet competition from new carriers.

In its petition, PLDT proposed cutting its international toll rates to the United States to 121.50 pesos from the present 152.55 pesos for the first three minutes. It also sought to lower call rates to other countries such as Hong Kong, Japan and Saudi Arabia, where many Filipinos work.

U.S. telephone companies have been pressing for a steep cut in international tariffs in a bid to generate more calls. At present, the rate between the United States and the Philippines is $1 per minute and U.S. firms have sought to cut it to 38 cents per minute.
PLDT has also sought rate increases for its basic local phone charges and plans to implement call metering to compensate for the international call reduction.
Sutherland said Asia Equity expects PLDT to post a net income of 7.2 billion pesos this year from 6.44 billion in 1996.
